units.name: mavsdk-core-runtime
units.description: This is the control center of the MAVSDK library - the code that defines what it means to 'connect to a drone' and to 'be a plugin' inside this SDK. An application creates one top-level SDK object, tells it to open a connection, and this unit turns that into a discovered 'System'. It also defines the contract every feature module must follow to plug into a system or act as a virtual vehicle component, tracks flight mode/autopilot brand/connection health, runs the heartbeat clock, can record traffic to a log file, and owns a handful of tiny shared plumbing types that almost every other unit is built on.
units.role: Defines System/Plugin/Connection and orchestrates the SDK's lifecycle and shared plumbing types.

depends_on.entrypoint: CallEveryHandler.add / change / reset / remove / remove_blocking / call_soon / run_once

effects.description: Constructs and owns UDP/TCP/serial/raw Connection objects and runs a dedicated asio io_context thread that drives their async I/O.
start_tlog_recording/stop_tlog_recording open, write and close a binary .tlog file recording all MAVLink traffic.
Reads MAVSDK_CALLBACK_DEBUGGING, MAVSDK_MESSAGE_DEBUGGING and MAVSDK_SYSTEM_DEBUGGING via getenv.
Drives heartbeat scheduling (1 Hz), the heartbeat watchdog, .tlog timestamping, callback-duration stats, and the timers-poll loop.
Owns and manages background threads: a dedicated io_context thread and a user-callback delivery thread.

units.name: mavlink-transport
units.description: This is the part of the drone software toolkit that opens the actual network or serial connections to a drone or companion computer, and turns the raw stream of bytes flowing over them into individual MAVLink messages. It supports UDP, TCP (connecting or listening), a serial cable, or an in-memory 'raw bytes' channel. It also does the low-level bookkeeping MAVLink needs internally. Everything else that talks to a vehicle sits on top of this layer.
units.role: Opens the wire (UDP/TCP/serial/raw) and turns bytes into MAVLink messages.

effects.description: Opens/binds UDP sockets, connects/listens TCP sockets, sends/receives datagrams/bytes asynchronously.
Opens a serial device path and configures it.
Performs blocking DNS/hostname lookups via getaddrinfo.
Reads MAVSDK_MAVLINK_DIRECT_DEBUGGING, MAVSDK_DROP_DEBUGGING, MAVSDK_MESSAGE_HANDLER_DEBUGGING via getenv.
Uses steady_clock to time out inactive UDP peers and for drop-rate diagnostics.
asio_throw_exception.cpp calls std::terminate() as Asio's required exception hook.

units.name: mavlink-protocol
units.description: This unit implements MAVLink's higher-level 'conversation rules' on top of raw message sending/receiving: sending a command and retrying until acknowledged, answering commands addressed to this component, getting/setting autopilot parameters (client and server sides), detecting a remote system is alive via heartbeats, keeping clocks in sync, ping round-trips, and assembling chunked status text into readable log lines.
units.role: Command/ack, parameter get-set, heartbeat, timesync and statustext protocol semantics.

entrypoints.name: CallEveryHandler.add / change / reset / remove / remove_blocking / call_soon / run_once

effects.description: TimeoutHandler and CallEveryHandler drive all retries and periodic sends (command retransmission, PING/TIMESYNC ticks, parameter retries).
Timesync computes and applies a clock offset between local and autopilot time.
MAVSDK_COMMAND_DEBUGGING and MAVSDK_PARAMETER_DEBUGGING read via getenv().
No sockets, files, subprocess, or random-number use; sequence/id fields are monotonic counters, not randomized.

units.name: mavlink-transfer-protocols
units.description: This unit implements two reliable 'chunked' delivery protocols riding on top of ordinary MAVLink messages: an FTP-like protocol for files on the vehicle's filesystem, and a mission-transfer protocol for sending/fetching an ordered list of waypoints. Both come in a client half and a server half, and both are self-contained state machines that split payloads into numbered chunks, retry on timeout, and report progress. Also includes the checksum helper used to verify a transferred file wasn't corrupted.
units.role: Reliable chunked file and mission-plan transfer over MAVLink, plus file checksumming.

effects.description: Reads and writes local files/directories to implement FTP-style download/upload/list/remove/rename/mkdir/rmdir.
Sends/receives MAVLink FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL and mission-related messages via the core message queue/handler registration.
Uses timeout handlers and a steady timer to detect lost packets and drive retries.
Reads MAVSDK_FTP_DEBUGGING to enable verbose logging.

units.name: core-utils
units.description: Small reusable helpers - encoding text, reading/writing files, geometry/math, downloading over HTTP, decompressing archives, and printing timestamped log messages - that other parts of the SDK use so they don't reinvent them. None of this code understands drones or MAVLink; it just provides generic building blocks.
units.role: Generic leaf infra: logging, base64, filesystem/cache, HTTP download, LZMA decompress, geometry/math/string helpers, time.

effects.description: Writes formatted, colorized log lines to stderr (or Android logcat), gated by a user-installable callback.
Uses time()/localtime() for log timestamps; wraps steady_clock/system_clock for elapsed-time and sleeping.
Reads HOME/TMPDIR env vars, creates cache/tmp directories, reads/writes/removes cache files with cross-process locks; LZMA decompression opens source/destination files directly.
Generates a random suffix for temporary directory names.
Performs blocking HTTP(S) downloads via libcurl on a dedicated background worker thread.

units.name: plugins-flight-mission
units.description: Lets an application tell the drone where to go and what to do: simple commands like arm, takeoff, land, return-to-launch and go-to-location; pre-planned multi-waypoint missions (including uploading/downloading raw mission items and importing QGroundControl/Mission Planner plan files); live streamed position/velocity/attitude setpoints for direct low-level flight control; manual joystick-style stick input; automatic following of a moving target; virtual no-fly-zone geofence boundaries; and the companion-computer counterparts of the action and raw-mission plugins.
units.role: Commands and navigates the vehicle: arm/takeoff/land, missions, offboard setpoints, manual control, follow-me, geofence.

entrypoints.name: Action
entrypoints.plain: arm(), takeoff(), land(), return_to_launch(), goto_location(), do_orbit().

effects.description: MissionRaw's QGroundControl/Mission Planner import reads a local .plan/.waypoints file from disk before parsing it into mission items.
Offboard uses the core Time abstraction to timestamp a watchdog grace period for setpoint streaming.

units.name: plugins-telemetry-sensing
units.description: Lets an application read the drone's live status - position, orientation, battery, GPS quality, whether it's flying - and also lets the drone (or a simulated/companion server) publish that same kind of status back out. It also receives outside data: nearby aircraft positions from an ADS-B transponder, precision GPS correction data (RTK), and external motion-tracking (mocap) position/velocity input used where GPS isn't available.
units.role: Reads and publishes live vehicle state and external sensor feeds.

effects.description: TelemetryServer computes a synthetic boot time from steady_clock for outgoing messages; Mocap converts timestamps into MAVLink message fields.
Rtk base64-decodes incoming RTCM correction payloads before fragmenting them into MAVLink messages.

units.name: plugins-payload
units.description: Lets an application control the camera and gimbal mounted on the drone, and operate cargo-handling equipment like a gripper claw or a winch. It also lets a drone advertise its own camera capabilities to a ground station via the camera-server plugin, and lets an application pull a live stream of the flight controller's internal log data for real-time diagnostics.
units.role: Controls camera, gimbal, and cargo/winch payload equipment; streams onboard logs live.

effects.description: Camera creates a temp download directory and a persistent file cache, writes downloaded camera-definition XML and photo files to disk.
Camera downloads camera-definition XML files over plain HTTP via a curl-based downloader.
Camera and CameraServer exchange RTSP stream URIs as strings inside MAVLink messages; MAVSDK itself does not open a video/RTSP connection.
Camera, Gimbal and LogStreaming each read a debug-enable environment variable at startup.
CameraServer runs a sleep-based loop thread to emit tracking-status messages at a fixed interval.

units.name: plugins-vehicle-config
units.description: Lets an application read and change the drone's stored settings, run sensor calibration routines, play alert tunes, deliberately simulate failures for testing, look up basic vehicle identity/flight-time info, send free-form status text as a simulated vehicle, and decide whether the vehicle is allowed to arm. This is the 'configure and administer the vehicle' side of the SDK.
units.role: Configures, calibrates, and administers the vehicle: parameters, calibration, tune, failure injection, info, arm authorization.

effects.description: Failure/Info busy-wait with short sleeps for state to arrive; Calibration::cancel() blocks on a promise/future.

units.name: plugins-connectivity-data
units.description: Lets an application move files and log data to and from the drone, open a remote command shell on it, send or receive MAVLink messages that don't have a dedicated feature, discover what a connected component is capable of, and receive event notifications from it. Also includes the shared core helper that fetches a component's self-described capability metadata over HTTP or MAVLink FTP, since that helper is only used by the component-metadata and events plugins in this group.
units.role: Raw connectivity and data exchange: file/log transfer, shell, raw MAVLink passthrough, capability discovery, events.

entrypoints.name: MavlinkComponentMetadata
entrypoints.plain: Core helper that fetches and caches a component's capability-metadata files over HTTP or MAVLink FTP.

effects.description: LogFiles writes downloaded vehicle log data to a local file; ComponentMetadataServer writes metadata JSON files to a temp directory it creates and removes; MavlinkComponentMetadata caches downloaded metadata files locally.
MavlinkDirect(Server) reads MAVSDK_MAVLINK_DIRECT_DEBUGGING; ComponentMetadataServer reads MAVSDK_COMPONENT_METADATA_DEBUGGING.
MavlinkComponentMetadata performs plain HTTP downloads of metadata files in addition to MAVLink-FTP downloads.

units.name: mavsdk-server
units.description: A background program (mavsdk_server) that lets programming languages other than C++ - Python, Kotlin, Java - remote-control a drone through MAVSDK. Instead of linking the C++ core+plugins directly, those languages talk to this program over a local network connection using gRPC. This unit is the translator: it takes an incoming network request, calls the real C++ plugin code, and translates the result or an ongoing stream of updates back into a network response. It covers the startup/shutdown C API and CLI binary, the gRPC server itself, one adapter class per feature, and the generated protobuf/gRPC wire-format glue code for each of those features.
units.role: gRPC daemon exposing the C++ core and every plugin to non-C++ language bindings over the network.

entrypoints.name: mavsdk_server_bin
entrypoints.plain: The standalone daemon executable other language bindings launch as a subprocess.

entrypoints.name: Per-plugin gRPC services (ActionService, TelemetryService, CameraService, MissionService, ...)

effects.description: Runs a gRPC server bound to 0.0.0.0:<port> (default 50051) - this IS the network server other language bindings connect to.
Builds a standalone executable meant to be launched as a subprocess by non-C++ bindings.
Parses argv for connection URL, gRPC port, MAVLink sysid/compid, and heartbeat watchdog timeout; writes usage/error text to stdout.

units.name: c-binding
units.description: This is the C-language front door to MAVSDK. It lets programs written in plain C control a drone through MAVSDK, by wrapping the SDK's C++ classes in ordinary C functions and structs. A small hand-written core (creating a connection, finding a drone/'system', logging) is paired with one wrapper file-pair per drone capability - roughly 36 pairs, automatically produced by a code generator that reads the same proto definitions used elsewhere in the project and stamps out matching C code from templates, so the C API always mirrors what the C++ API offers.
units.role: Generated C API wrapping the C++ core and every plugin, plus the generator that produces it.

entrypoints.name: mavsdk_<plugin>_* for each of the remaining ~35 generated plugins
entrypoints.plain: One generated set of C functions per drone capability, mirroring the C++ plugin class.

effects.description: The generator scripts write generated .h/.cpp plugin wrapper files and a generated CMake file into c/src/.
The generator shells out to protoc (with a custom plugin backend) and to python3/pip to run the code generator.
The runtime C wrapper functions perform no direct network/disk/clock I/O themselves - they only translate C calls into calls on the C++ core and plugin objects.

units.name: jni-binding
units.description: This is the translation layer that lets programs written in Java or Kotlin (running on the JVM, e.g. Android apps) call the drone SDK's native code. For each feature there is a small Java class declaring 'native' methods, and a matching C++ file that receives the call from Java, converts arguments, forwards the call into the SDK's C-language API, and converts any result or callback back into something Java understands. Almost all of this bridging code is generated from templates using the same proto definitions used elsewhere, so the same shape of code is produced for all ~37 plugins. A handful of hand-written core bridge files (creating the SDK instance, connections, systems, logging, configuration) glue everything together.
units.role: Generated JNI bridge exposing the C API to Java/Kotlin, plus the generator that produces it and its build/validation scripts.

entrypoints.name: NativeAction.armAsync / .takeoffAsync / .landAsync (representative of ~37 generated per-plugin Native<Plugin> classes)

effects.description: Attaches/detaches native SDK callback threads to the JVM so C++ callbacks can call back into Java across threads the JVM doesn't own.
The generator scripts shell out to protoc and to python3/pip to run the code generator, and jvm build/validate scripts shell out to javac and nm.
The generator writes generated *_jni.cpp/Native*.java files and a generated CMake file to disk; validate_generated.py reads the generated files back to cross-check them.

units.name: kotlin-binding
units.description: This is the Kotlin toolkit that lets Kotlin, JVM, and Android applications control a drone using idiomatic Kotlin code (classes, coroutines, reactive data streams) instead of talking to the native code directly. It provides the main entry class for connecting to a drone and one class per drone feature. Almost all of the per-feature code is regenerated from the project's shared proto definitions by a template-based code generator, so the Kotlin API always matches whatever the SDK exposes. Under the hood, every one of these classes forwards calls down into the JNI bridge layer that talks to the SDK's native code; this unit itself does no networking of its own, aside from locating and loading the native library.
units.role: Generated Kotlin Multiplatform API wrapping the JNI bridge, plus the generator that produces it.

entrypoints.name: SystemPlugins/ServerComponentPlugins accessors, one per generated plugin class (Action, Telemetry, Camera, Mission, Param, and ~30 more)

depends_on.entrypoint: NativeAction.armAsync / .takeoffAsync / .landAsync (representative of ~37 generated per-plugin Native<Plugin> classes)

effects.description: Loads the native JNI bridge shared library via System.loadLibrary/System.load, reading OS name/arch properties to pick the right binary variant.
On the JVM target, extracts the native library from a JAR resource to a temp file when it isn't already on the library path.

Uses ReentrantReadWriteLock and kotlinx.coroutines callbackFlow/awaitClose to bridge native async callbacks into Kotlin Flows/suspend functions; all actual drone communication happens on the native/JNI side.
The generator shells out to protoc/python3 to regenerate the per-plugin Kotlin files from proto definitions.

units.concerns: This unit's full generated file set numbers roughly 92 Kotlin files (one pair per plugin across commonMain and jvmAndroidMain, following the exact pattern of Action.kt/ActionNative.kt shown here); only a representative subset is enumerated above for manifest size, since .kt files are not part of this checkout's mechanically-checked source-extension set.

units.name: python-sync-binding
units.description: This is the Python package (published as 'mavsdk' on PyPI) that lets a Python program control a drone through MAVSDK. It is a ctypes wrapper: at import time it searches the filesystem for a native shared library (built from the C API) and loads it directly into the Python process. Every operation - creating a connection, arming a drone, reading telemetry, running a mission - is a direct call from Python into that native library. It also includes one generated Python module per drone capability, produced from proto definitions by a template-based code generator.
units.role: ctypes wrapper exposing the C API as a Python package, plus the generator that produces its per-plugin modules.

entrypoints.name: mavsdk.plugins.<name>.<Name> for each of the remaining 35 generated plugins

effects.description: cmavsdk_loader.py searches package/cwd 'lib' directories via pathlib for the native shared library file before loading it with ctypes.CDLL.
Loads the native shared library via ctypes.CDLL and calls C functions on it directly; all MAVLink/network I/O happens inside that native library, not in this Python code.
Prints library search progress to stdout; registers atexit cleanup to release native handles on interpreter exit.
The generator script (tools/generate_from_protos.bash) shells out to protoc/pip/venv to regenerate the plugin modules; a maintainer-only codegen path, not run at import time.

units.concerns: This package does NOT talk to mavsdk_server over gRPC despite the name suggesting a network client - it loads a native shared library via ctypes and calls the C API directly, so its real infra dependency is c-binding, not mavsdk-server.

units.name: python-async-binding
units.description: This is the 'aiomavsdk' Python package: it lets a Python program written with async/await control a drone using the same feature set as the plain 'mavsdk' package, but with a coding style that fits into modern async Python applications. It does this by wrapping every class and function of the 'mavsdk' package directly: quick calls become 'async def' methods, potentially slow calls run in a background thread so they don't freeze the event loop, and event subscriptions become 'async for' loops. It does not talk to the drone itself - it borrows the mavsdk package's own connection to the vehicle and adds an asyncio-friendly layer on top.
units.role: asyncio wrapper around the python-sync-binding package, plus the generator that produces its per-plugin modules.

entrypoints.name: aiomavsdk.plugins.<name>.<Name>Async for each of the remaining 34 plugins

effects.description: Every wrapper method runs the underlying blocking mavsdk call on a background thread via asyncio's run_in_executor so the event loop is not blocked.

Streaming subscriptions register a callback that pushes onto an asyncio.Queue via call_soon_threadsafe, then expose the queue as an async generator - the only 'I/O-like' mechanism implemented in this package itself.
The generator script shells out to protoc/pip/venv to regenerate the plugin modules; a maintainer-only codegen path, not run at import time.

units.concerns: This package has no networking of its own - it is a pure async-wrapper layer that imports and calls into the python-sync-binding package's classes directly (confirmed in all core and plugin files), making that a hard in-repo code dependency rather than a wire-protocol boundary.
